final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to the same conditional position already reflected in the initial audit: overall readiness evidence is positive, but the present record still lacks proof that current release documentation reflects the current regression or that approved mitigation/risk acceptance exists. That distinction matters. A caveated compliance verdict would require evidence that the caveat has actually been operationalized through current documentation or approval. Here, the Actor only argued that such a path exists in principle. Because the unresolved compliance predicate remains unresolved on the present record, the packet is still plausibly supportable in part but not adequately supported for current certification as submitted.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results for the legal intake triage regression.
No admissible evidence shows the legal intake triage weakness is explicitly disclosed in current release materials for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering launch with this current subgroup weakness.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for disclosure or approved mitigation.
Prior approval and the informal monitoring note remain contextual only and cannot carry the current certification decision.
